notes: Identity assessment: substantial article-body web parse, including analytical sections, Table 1, figure captions, discussion, footnotes and references; not merely an abstract or preregistration. The first-person money-priming bias analyses responding to Rohrer et al. (2015) and Vohs (2015) are substantively consistent with the neutral Vadillo, Hardwicke, and Shanks (2016) reference. However, the supplied parse lacks its article title, byline, and own DOI, so exact title/author/DOI identity cannot be independently confirmed. Figure assets named xge_145_5_655_fig1a support consistency with volume/issue/start page, but do not establish authorship. Source identity remains provisional. No PDF supplied; no numeric field promoted. All four assigned rows have null study/description and empty original locators. The common paper reference cannot distinguish multiple data sets, outcomes, or statistical tests. Do not assign the four data sets to four IDs by their order or count. No row-specific target can be established; source identity is additionally provisional. Unassigned candidates: Egger regressions: Vohs et al. (2006)/Caruso et al. (2013), t(12) = 5.42, p < .001; Rohrer et al. (2015)/Klein et al. (2014), t(40) = 1.48, p = .15; Vohs (2015) Table 1, t(18) = 3.87, p = .001; Vohs (2015) Table 2, t(21) = 1.89, p = .072. These are printed t statistics, not converted standardized effects. p-Curve Analysis: main/robustness Stouffer z = −4.06 and −5.16, each p < .0001; nonparametric binomial p = .266 and .168; flatness binomial p = .032 and .076. Table 1 has further excess-significance tests for four data sets under three power definitions. N candidates: four main-text Rohrer experiments, two appendix experiments, 36 Many Labs data points; no row-specific analytic N established. No N derived from df and no sums performed. Dependent effects were restricted to the first effect per study for the funnel analyses. Footnote 1 describes inaccessible underlying reports, omission of two Chatterjee data points, and recomputation of effect sizes. The p-curve pooled available significant contrasts and used different main/robustness selections. No common analytic N is justified for unspecified tests.
